newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE states 'extreme concern' about Yugo election.
newsitem.headline: OSCE states 'extreme concern' about Yugo election.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Thursday it was "extremely concerned" about irregularities and shortcomings during federal and municipal elections held in Yugoslavia earlier this month.

"The Chairman-in-Office is extremely concerned about the shortcomings, irregularities and violations of law which occurred during the vote verification process, after results of the second round had already been tabulated at the polling station level, and during the review of complaints procedure," the Vienna-based OSCE said in a statement.

A group of opposition parties has said it won municipal elections in 15 of Serbia's 18 largest towns including Belgrade, but electoral commissions overturned the results in most towns claiming unspecified irregularities.

Reruns took place on Wednesday in several cities but were boycotted by the opposition, which has staged an unprecedented wave of mass protests for the past 10 days against the hardline regime of Socialist President Slobodan Milosevic.

"It is puzzling to see that the third round of the elections took place especially in those constituencies where the political opposition had won strong positions," the OSCE said, citing Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, the body's Chairman-in-Office.

The OSCE added that the integrity of the entire election process remained under question until an independent review of the election could be undertaken and said it was ready to offer its assistance in that process if required.
